31: /-- The empty (heterogeneous) relation, which always returns `False`. -/
32: @[nolint unusedArguments]
33: def emptyHRelation {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} (_ : α) (_ : β) := False
34: 
35: /-- Domain of a relation. -/
36: def dom (r : α → β → Prop) : Set α := {a | ∃ b, r a b}
37: 
38: /-- Codomain of a relation, aka range. -/
39: def cod (r : α → β → Prop) : Set β := {b | ∃ a, r a b}
40: 
41: /-- The join of the reflexive transitive closure. This is not named in Mathlib, but see
42:   `#loogle Relation.Join (Relation.ReflTransGen ?r)` -/
43: abbrev MJoin (r : α → α → Prop) := Join (ReflTransGen r)
44: 
45: /-- The relation `r` 'up to' the relation `s`. -/
46: def UpTo (r s : α → α → Prop) : α → α → Prop := Comp s (Comp r s)
47: 
48: /-- A relation `r` is (right) Euclidean if `r a b` and `r a c` guarantee `r b c`. -/
49: class RightEuclidean (r : α → α → Prop) where
50:   rightEuclidean : r a b → r a c → r b c
51: 
52: /-- A relation `r` is (left) Euclidean if `r a c` and `r b c` guarantee `r a b`. -/
53: class LeftEuclidean (r : α → α → Prop) where
54:   leftEuclidean {a b c} : r a c → r b c → r a b
55: 
56: /-- A relation has the diamond property when all reductions with a common origin are joinable -/
57: abbrev Diamond (r : α → α → Prop) := ∀ {a b c : α}, r a b → r a c → Join r b c
58: 
59: /-- A relation is confluent when its reflexive transitive closure has the diamond property. -/
60: abbrev Confluent (r : α → α → Prop) := Diamond (ReflTransGen r)
61: 
62: /-- A relation is semi-confluent when single and multiple steps with common origin
63:   are multi-joinable. -/
64: abbrev SemiConfluent (r : α → α → Prop) :=
65:   ∀ {x y₁ y₂}, ReflTransGen r x y₂ → r x y₁ → Join (ReflTransGen r) y₁ y₂
66: 
67: /-- A relation has the Church Rosser property when equivalence implies multi-joinability. -/
68: abbrev ChurchRosser (r : α → α → Prop) := ∀ {x y}, EqvGen r x y → Join (ReflTransGen r) x y
69: 
70: /-- An element is reducible with respect to a relation if there is a value it is related to. -/
71: abbrev Reducible (r : α → α → Prop) (x : α) : Prop := ∃ y, r x y
72: 
73: /-- A relation `r` is serial if every element is `Reducible`, i.e. `Relator.LeftTotal`. -/
74: class Serial (r : α → α → Prop) where
75:   serial : Relator.LeftTotal r
76: 
77: /-- An element is normal if it is not reducible. -/
78: abbrev Normal (r : α → α → Prop) (x : α) : Prop := ¬ Reducible r x
79: 
80: /-- An element is normalizable if it is related to a normal element. -/
81: abbrev Normalizable (r : α → α → Prop) (x : α) : Prop :=
82:   ∃ n, ReflTransGen r x n ∧ Normal r n
83: 
84: /-- A relation is normalizing when every element is normalizable. -/
85: abbrev Normalizing (r : α → α → Prop) : Prop :=
86:   ∀ x, Normalizable r x
87: 
88: /-- An element `x` is `SN` (for strongly-normalising) for a relation `r` if it is accessible under
89: the inverse of `r`. -/
90: abbrev SN (r : α → α → Prop) := Acc (fun a b => r b a)
91: 
92: /-- A relation is acyclic if its transitive closure is irreflexive, equivalently if it admits no
93: nonempty cycle. -/
94: abbrev Acyclic (r : α → α → Prop) := Std.Irrefl (TransGen r)
95: 
96: /-- A relation is terminating when the inverse of its transitive closure is well-founded.
97:   Note that this is also called Noetherian or strongly normalizing in the literature. -/
98: abbrev Terminating (r : α → α → Prop) := WellFounded (fun a b => r b a)
99: 
100: /-- A relation is convergent when it is both confluent and terminating. -/
101: abbrev Convergent (r : α → α → Prop) := Confluent r ∧ Terminating r
102: 
103: /-- A relation is locally confluent when all reductions with a common origin are multi-joinable -/
104: abbrev LocallyConfluent (r : α → α → Prop) :=
105:   ∀ {a b c : α}, r a b → r a c → Join (ReflTransGen r) b c
106: 
107: /-- A relation is strongly confluent when single steps are reflexive- and multi-joinable. -/
108: abbrev StronglyConfluent (r : α → α → Prop) :=
109:   ∀ {x y₁ y₂}, r x y₁ → r x y₂ → ∃ z, ReflGen r y₁ z ∧ ReflTransGen r y₂ z
110: 
111: /-- Generalization of `Confluent` to two relations. -/
112: def Commute (r₁ r₂ : α → α → Prop) := ∀ {x y₁ y₂},
113:   ReflTransGen r₁ x y₁ → ReflTransGen r₂ x y₂ → ∃ z, ReflTransGen r₂ y₁ z ∧ ReflTransGen r₁ y₂ z
114: 
115: /-- Generalization of `StronglyConfluent` to two relations. -/
116: def StronglyCommute (r₁ r₂ : α → α → Prop) :=
117:   ∀ {x y₁ y₂}, r₁ x y₁ → r₂ x y₂ → ∃ z, ReflGen r₂ y₁ z ∧ ReflTransGen r₁ y₂ z
118: 
119: /-- Generalization of `Diamond` to two relations. -/
120: def DiamondCommute (r₁ r₂ : α → α → Prop) :=
121:   ∀ {x y₁ y₂}, r₁ x y₁ → r₂ x y₂ → ∃ z, r₂ y₁ z ∧ r₁ y₂ z
122: 
123: /-- A pair of subrelations lifts to transitivity on the relation. -/
124: @[implicit_reducible]
125: def transLeftRight (s s' r : α → α → Prop) [IsTrans α r] (h : s ≤ r) (h' : s' ≤ r) :
126:     Trans s s' r where
127:   trans hab hbc := _root_.trans (h _ _ hab) (h' _ _ hbc)
128: 
129: /-- A subrelation lifts to transitivity on the left of the relation. -/
130: @[implicit_reducible]
131: def transLeft (s r : α → α → Prop) [IsTrans α r] (h : s ≤ r) : Trans s r r where
132:   trans hab hbc := _root_.trans (h _ _ hab) hbc
133: 
134: /-- A subrelation lifts to transitivity on the right of the relation. -/
135: @[implicit_reducible]
136: def transRight (s r : α → α → Prop) [IsTrans α r] (h : s ≤ r) : Trans r s r where
137:   trans hab hbc := _root_.trans hab (h _ _ hbc)
138: 
139: end Relation
